investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because no VM is ever assigned, the eval runner never receives a vmId or a remoteState value, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256) cannot be satisfied. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the 6-node cluster. No capacity was reclaimed before the probe timeout, and preemption found no evictable pods.

Secondary: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated. If the affinity were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, scheduling could succeed.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have left remote-agent VMs running and not cleaned them up, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.
Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event, node drain, or node failure may have reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule even one probe pod.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-16T18:43–18:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label have exhausted their peer-pod VM quota (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful). The pod remained Unschedulable for 142 seconds before the eval timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state check to fail its expected-output contract. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM quota on the 2 nodes that carry the kata runtime class — the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, meaning the extended resource count is at or above the node's declared capacity. This is the strongest evidence-backed cause.

Insufficient nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity or node selector — 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, leaving only the 2 kata-capable nodes, both of which are resource-exhausted. If the affinity rules were relaxed or more kata-capable nodes were available, scheduling might succeed.

Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all available peer-pod VM slots — if other agents or eval runs were active at the same time, they may have consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota before this eval's pod was submitted.

Cluster autoscaler not adding kata-capable nodes in time — if autoscaling is configured, it may not have provisioned a new kata node within the eval's timeout window, or kata-capable node pools may not be part of the autoscaler group.
Node affinity/selector misconfiguration — the pod's affinity rules may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run the workload even without the kata runtime class.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because no VM is ever assigned, the eval runner never receives a vmId or a remoteState value, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256) cannot be satisfied. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduling failure message, pod unscheduled for 147s, latencyMs=153578
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the pod never reaching a running VM

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256-259): contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because no VM was provisioned
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=129486, endedAt=2026-07-16T18:43:40.059Z — the probe timed out waiting for scheduling, not for an API error
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which depends on a schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm node to return a vmId
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the 6-node cluster. No capacity was reclaimed before the probe timeout, and preemption found no evictable pods.

Secondary: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated. If the affinity were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, scheduling could succeed.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have left remote-agent VMs running and not cleaned them up, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain occupied.
Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event, node drain, or node failure may have reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule even one probe pod.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a misconfigured node selector or affinity rule.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded and returned all required evidence, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add a cluster node health eval that verifies the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-labeled nodes are Ready, catching node drain or failure events before they exhaust scheduling capacity for remote-agent probes.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-16T18:43–18:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production cluster. Two nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label have exhausted their peer-pod VM quota (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also ruled out (no preemption victims found, preemption not helpful). The pod remained Unschedulable for 142 seconds before the eval timed out. Because agent creation never completed, the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state check to fail its expected-output contract. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:180-188: remote-agent-state is marked required=true; degradedAfterFailures=1 means a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature.
possibleCauses: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM quota on the 2 nodes that carry the kata runtime class — the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, meaning the extended resource count is at or above the node's declared capacity. This is the strongest evidence-backed cause.

Insufficient nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity or node selector — 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, leaving only the 2 kata-capable nodes, both of which are resource-exhausted. If the affinity rules were relaxed or more kata-capable nodes were available, scheduling might succeed.

Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all available peer-pod VM slots — if other agents or eval runs were active at the same time, they may have consumed the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota before this eval's pod was submitted.

Cluster autoscaler not adding kata-capable nodes in time — if autoscaling is configured, it may not have provisioned a new kata node within the eval's timeout window, or kata-capable node pools may not be part of the autoscaler group.
Node affinity/selector misconfiguration — the pod's affinity rules may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run the workload even without the kata runtime class.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain unscheduled until the eval timeout. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-runtime check produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out before the VM is ready, preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, state-polling, or runtime-chat steps. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval suite in production-api.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes and making the capacity problem worse.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or production workload may have left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 kata nodes, consuming the vm resource slots without releasing them (no cleanup evidence is available to confirm or deny this).

Lower probability — the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit was recently reduced, shrinking available capacity below what the eval suite requires (no quota-change evidence is present in the packet).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the production Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used counts on the 2 eligible nodes. Identify which pods are consuming the slots.
If orphaned eval pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, terminate them and verify that the resource is released. Re-run the eval suite to confirm recovery.

If production workloads are consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, assess whether the node pool needs to be scaled out (add more kata-capable nodes) or whether the eval suite needs a dedicated resource quota.

Investigate why 4 of 6 nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. Determine if this is intentional topology or a misconfiguration that is unnecessarily concentrating scheduling pressure on 2 nodes.

Review whether the eval cleanup path (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after each eval run, especially on failure paths where the pod never became ready.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true (features.json lines 183-184) and degradedAfterFailures=1, confirm the feature health status reflects degraded/outage correctly and that on-call is aware if this is a sustained failure.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to confirm persistence of scheduling failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is still present. A pass would indicate capacity was restored; a fail with the same message confirms the cluster state has not changed.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Compare latencyMs and scheduler message verbatim against failed-check.message evidence.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and allocatable on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the 2 kata-capable nodes have exhausted their VM slots and identifies which pods are holding them. This is the fastest way to confirm or rule out resource exhaustion as the root cause.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all running remote-agent pods and their resource consumption on the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether orphaned eval pods or production workloads are occupying the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, which would explain why no capacity is available for new eval pods.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Verify node affinity labels on all 6 cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that exactly 2 nodes carry the label required by remote-agent pods, establishing the true schedulable node count and whether the affinity configuration is intentional or a misconfiguration.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks in isolation after any capacity remediation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: These are required checks (required=true per features.json line 183-184). Confirming they pass after capacity is restored validates that the scheduling fix resolves the full feature degradation, not just the runtime check.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or equivalent tooling shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available (allocatable > 0) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the next eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request on the pod spec) would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes on a subsequent run while kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity remains at zero, the scheduling error message would be a false positive and the real failure would be elsewhere.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass, the root cause would be localized to the runtime step rather than pod scheduling, and the kata capacity explanation would not apply.
If an eval run with a different orgId or token succeeds while this one fails, the issue could be org-scoped quota or permission rather than cluster-wide capacity.

If the cluster shows that all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are free but the pod still fails to schedule, the node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 nodes would become the primary cause rather than resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that asserts kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is above a minimum threshold before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct, actionable signal rather than a timeout.
Add an eval that monitors the count of running remote-agent pods and alerts when it approaches the kata.peerpods.io/vm node limit, providing early warning before capacity is fully exhausted.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval cycle, catching resource leaks before they accumulate.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod selector meets a minimum (e.g., at least 3 nodes), catching topology misconfigurations before they reduce the schedulable pool to a single point of failure.
